fieldValues.title: Working groups and delegation
fieldValues.body:
The owner cannot judge every merge. So the owner **delegates**: a working group gets a mandate, decides and merges inside it, and reports back. Anything outside the mandate comes back to the owner as one proposed decision. This is how a co-op runs a subcommittee. ```mermaid flowchart TD OW["Owner role
(the programme's top authority)"] -->|delegates| GR["Group role
purpose, mandate, charter fields"] CD["Charter decision
ratified in an owner session"] -.->|puts in force| GR GR --> SO["Standing orders
membership and quorum, cycle and report,
budget, reporting and minutes"] GR --> CP["Compass
boundary, tensions, this-over-that leanings"] GR --> MB["Members, each authorised-by the role
steward, builder, reviewer, analyst"] GR --> LOG["The group's own decision log"] MB -->|"cycle report"| OW ``` **What a group has.** A purpose; standing orders; a delegation order (what it decides, what it escalates); a compass; membership and quorum; a rhythm with a cycle and a budget; its own decision log; and a duty to report. All of it is records in srs-programme. The numbers that code needs (label, quorum seats, budget per cycle, cycle close, pause limit, governed repos) are fields on the group role, read by `clerk groups`. Nothing is hard-coded. **Inside or outside the mandate.** ```mermaid flowchart TD Q["Work or a question
in the group's issues"] --> M{"Inside the mandate?
executes a recorded ruling,
in the group's repos, within budget"} M -->|yes| G["Builder builds, reviewer reviews
quorum comment, pr-upkeep merges"] G --> L["Decision proposed in the group log;
the group's session ratifies it at cycle close"] M -->|"no: new ruling, breaking change,
gate or merge rules, over budget"| X["One proposed decision to the owner
(fact, why it matters, options, recommendation)"] L --> RP[Cycle report] X --> RP RP --> OS["Owner session: receives the report,
ratifies or sets aside the escalation"] ``` **Quorum and merge.** A group PR merges only when a builder and a *different* reviewer agree after the last commit, the gates are green, the cycle's budget is not spent and the group is not paused. The reviewer posts a `` comment; `pr-upkeep` checks it every 15 minutes and merges. A new commit voids the quorum. **Pause.** If the owner leaves two cycle reports unacknowledged, the group pauses: no new builds and no group merges, though reviews and escalations continue. Silence slows the group down rather than letting it run unwatched. **The central group.** Work with no `wg:` label belongs to the central group, SemanticOps, held by the Owner role. Its seats are the owner's builder and reviewer, plus agents `authorised-by` the Owner role, such as the nightly `agent:unattended-worker`. The central group never claims a delegated group's work. **Groups today.** WG Third-party ready (semanticops.com#31, `wg:third-party-ready`) is in force. WG Agent-supported editor (semanticops.com#29, `wg:agent-editor`) has been chartered as records. A new group is chartered only on a trigger: a steady ready queue that needs delegated merges. **Chartering.** `clerk charter` writes the whole charter as drafts and a proposed decision; an owner session ratifies it and asserts `delegates`. The steps are in stage 10. The briefs the members follow: [routines/working-groups.md](../routines/working-groups.md).
